request: owner: 'model should be machine learning in order to be less wrong — LINEAR REGRESSION'
method: Expanding-window walk-forward, date-ordered, on the frozen as-of features.csv (no look-ahead, no market prices as inputs). 1054 scored games after a 400-game burn-in. Compared against V13 on the SAME games via the frozen historical replay.
headline_finding: LINEAR REGRESSION IS THE WORST MODEL TESTED — Brier 0.2555, WORSE than simply predicting the league home-win rate (0.2501). The specific thing requested does not make the model less wrong; it makes it more wrong.
why: The target is binary. OLS on a 0/1 outcome (the Linear Probability Model) fits a straight line to a probability, so it pushes predictions toward and past the 0/1 boundary where the true response must flatten, and its errors are heteroscedastic by construction. Its accuracy (54.4%) is respectable — it ranks games acceptably — but its PROBABILITIES are poorly calibrated, and Brier and log loss both punish that. Logistic regression is the same idea with the correct link function.

logistic_vs_V13.verdict: NOT SIGNIFICANT — logistic does NOT beat V13; the two are indistinguishable on this sample

logistic_vs_base_rate.verdict: SIGNIFICANT, but marginally (CI barely excludes 0) and tiny in magnitude

V13_vs_base_rate.verdict: NOT significant — V13 still cannot be distinguished from the base rate

LPM_vs_base_rate.verdict: worse than base rate, not significantly so

honest_verdict: Fitting a model helped, but barely. The ONLY model that separates from the base rate at all is logistic regression, by 0.0035 Brier with a confidence interval that barely excludes zero. It does NOT beat V13. Nothing here is a validated edge, and none of it changes the gate.

what_the_coefficients_say.reading: Starting-pitcher quality dominates — its coefficient is 9x the team run-differential term. Park is second and NEGATIVE, i.e. hitter-friendly parks slightly favour the visitor once the starters are accounted for. Team offence is nearly worthless once SP and defence are in. This is a real, useful finding: the model's signal is concentrated in the starter, which is also the input most vulnerable to a late scratch.

calibration: Monotone across deciles at the extremes (bucket 1 pred .417/actual .358; bucket 10 pred .625/actual .638) but noisy in the middle (bucket 4 pred .511/actual .434; bucket 5 pred .526/actual .600). The model has some genuine ranking ability at the tails and essentially none in the middle.
limits: Trained on 1475 games from ONE partial season — small for 7 features.
features.csv ends 2026-07-19, so nothing after that is in training or scoring.
No market benchmark: prices are deliberately not inputs, and the 8/10 board is cross-book so it cannot supply one.
Beating a base rate is not an edge; beating the CLOSING PRICE after vig is, and that has not been demonstrated.
recommended_next: The gain is in features, not in the estimator. Bullpen quality, rest/travel, lineup handedness splits and confirmed-lineup data are absent, and the coefficients say the starter is where the signal lives — so starter-level detail (recent form, times-through-order, opponent handedness) is the highest-value addition. Swapping estimators again will not move this.
